content.comment_body: I'm working with the [product_name] module and Pt1000 probes. The probes are placed at some distance from the [product_name] base unit. The temperature readings I get are quite erratic, showing values like 25, 27, 24, 27, 25, 24, etc. How can I make these readings more consistent? Is it possible to add a capacitor between the input terminals or perhaps between the inputs and ground to help? Also, is there a way to compute an average value directly in the [product_name] system? Thank you.

Hello, It's best not to use a capacitor here, since the [product_name] module won't properly detect the sensor after power-up if you do. For [product_name] version [version_no], you can use the 'Analog Filter' function block. If you are using [product_name] version [version_no], visit [url] and look for the analog value stabilization example; it's found among the application examples on the right side of the webpage. Hopefully, this information resolves your issue.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers on achieving stable temperature measurements using a [product_name] module combined with Pt1000 probes in a remote configuration. The original poster explores hardware fixes like capacitors and software approaches such as averaging. Responses highlight the risks of hardware filtering and suggest using built-in software functions or official examples to stabilize analog readings, steering the solution towards reliable, built-in options.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to achieve consistently stable and reliable temperature measurements using built-in tools or recommended best practices for signal filtering or averaging within the [product_name] system.
